Across all 100 replications, the same three components (item, model$\times$item, residual) emerge as the top three (set consistency 100\%), with Kendall's $\tau = 0.81$ between binary and continuous rankings.

The generalizability coefficient differs by only 0.0008 ($G = 0.9361$ vs.\ $0.9369$), and all non-precision variance components differ by less than 2 percentage points. The 10pp increase in item variance share (58.4\% $\to$ 68.5\%) is fully explained by the removal of precision-related components ($\sim$4.5\% total), which redistributes across remaining sources. This confirms that the exp-002 design preserves the variance structure of the full crossing.

tool_args.old_string: Our findings are bounded by four scope constraints. First, the primary cross-model analysis covers eight open-weight 7--9B parameter instruction-tuned models; within-family scale validation extends to 3B--9B (Qwen2.5), but results do not generalize to API-based models (where infrastructure is opaque), base (non-instruction-tuned) models, models above 9B parameters, or domain-adapted fine-tuned variants. Extending this validation to larger scales (e.g., 70B+) remains for future work; larger models with higher accuracy could exhibit compressed item variance due to ceiling effects. Second, all experiments run on single-GPU inference (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000); multi-GPU tensor parallelism introduces additional numerical non-associativity that our design does not capture. Third, the benchmark sample covers three multiple-choice and two free-form tasks ($n = 5$); item-level variance patterns within each benchmark are well-powered, but the format-associated claim rests on a benchmark-level comparison with limited statistical power ($p = 0.10$, permutation test). Other evaluation formats such as code generation, long-form text production, and multi-turn dialogue may exhibit different variance structures. Fourth, all variance decompositions use binary (correct/incorrect) scoring. Partial-credit or rubric-based scoring could alter free-form variance structure---in particular, capturing chain-of-thought quality may redistribute residual variance (currently 40--44\% for FF) to item or model$\times$item components, potentially narrowing the format-associated gap. Two natural extensions remain: multi-GPU tensor parallelism (testing precision separability under distributed numerical non-associativity) and fine-tuning variance analysis (quantifying how adaptation reshapes item difficulty profiles).
